newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi to add 30 members to Shura council - paper.
newsitem.headline: Saudi to add 30 members to Shura council - paper.

text.p: A Saudi-owned newspaper said on Thursday Saudi Arabia would raise the number of delegates in its consultative Shura Council to 90 from 60, expanding popular participation in the country's first representative body.

The Arabic-language al-Hayat daily quoted council president Sheikh Mohammad bin Ibrahim bin Jubair as saying the number of members in the appointed council would be increased at the start of the new session, which begins on July 7.

The London-based paper quoted other sources as saying 30 additional members would join the council, and 30 of the current delegates would be replaced. It said an official announcement of the new membership was expected within days.

King Fahd in 1993 set up the consultative council, the kingdom's first representative body for almost 60 years, and created regional assemblies in 13 provinces, the first steps towards giving Saudis more say in running the country's affairs.
The Shura Council and the regional assemblies only have consultative powers.
Senior members of the royal family traditionally control the country's administration, occupying many top positions at national and provincial level.
The king promised after the 1990-91 Gulf crisis to gradually introduce political and economic reforms aimed at modernising the system of government.
King Fahd in January was quoted by Saudi media as saying the kingdom was examining how to develop political reforms including the Shura Council.
